newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Tivoli Gardens has second year of losses.
newsitem.headline: Danish Tivoli Gardens has second year of losses.

text.p: Denmark's Tivoli Gardens amusement park on Thursday reported a financial loss for the second year and said it would stay in the red next season.

Announcing 1995/96 net losses of 50.8 million crowns compared to a shortfall of 18.8 million last year, a statement said that Tivoli spent 50 million crowns on building, renovation and improvments aimed at reversing declining earnings.

"Even though the result appears discouraging at first glance, behind the figures there is a will to implement the changes necessary to turn round the disappointing developments of recent years," Managing Director Lars Liebst said.

"Expenditure of some 50 million crowns will create the room and the trading freedom that the new management needs in the present situation," he said, adding that he expected to return the world-famous site to financial health "within a few years."
The company brought in a new management team and devised a long-term development plan after falling into loss last year for the first time in its 154-year history.
It said it had a total of 3.1 million visitors during its summer season and Christmas market, comparable to the year before when adjusted for the 14-day shorter 1995/96 season.
